Layout after patching: 0x44B911 push esi (d); 0x44B912 call C3_SyncDelta, which returns to 0x44B917; 0x44B917 is the ORIGINAL 'add [0xDC7580],eax' kept in place; 0x44B91D-0x44B91E nop. C3_SyncDelta is pure asm, stdcall with one argument (ret 4). It returns the sync delta in EAX, may clobber ECX/EDX/flags, and preserves EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP. Code:
  mov  eax,[0x00DC7A8C]        ; v (ms per client frame, 33)
  imul eax,[esp+4]             ; P = v*d, bit-identical to the original 'imul eax,esi'
  cmp  byte [g_m60],0 / je .ret                     ; 30 mode: EAX = P (STOCK)
  mov  edx,fs:[0x24] / cmp edx,[g_mainTid] / jne .ret ; any other thread: stock
  cmp  byte [g_inB],0 / jne .flush
  cmp  dword [esp+4],0 / jle .flush                 ; A-render with d==0 (paused, frozen, halted): stock adds 0
  ; advancing A-render (d>0): add only half the step now (lag phase)
  mov  ecx,[g_syncHalfPar] / xor dword [g_syncHalfPar],1
  add  ecx,eax / sar ecx,1     ; h = (P+par)>>1 -> 16,17,16,... for P=33; always 0<=h<=P
  sub  eax,ecx                 ; P-h
  mov  edx,[g_syncOwed] / mov [g_syncOwed],eax      ; owed = P-h
  lea  eax,[edx+ecx] / ret 4   ; delta = previous owed (normally 0) + h
.flush:                        ; B-render (d is always 0 there), or a non-advancing A
  add  eax,[g_syncOwed] / mov dword [g_syncOwed],0 ; delta = P + owed
.ret: ret 4

Paths:
- 30-mode: delta = v*d. This equals the original, and the flags come from the kept add.
- 60 A-render: delta = h (plus any carry left over by a B-render that never reached here).
- 60 B-render: delta = owed, i.e. P_A - h, or 0 if the A-render did not advance.
Per pair the sum is exactly v*d, so [0xDC7580] equals stock at every logic step. Both the A-render and the B-render call WW3D::Sync, so the animation and snow clock advances on both: by h, then by P-h.

sites.purpose: Frame-triggered animation events in W3DModelDraw (W3DScriptedModelDraw/Horde/Quadruped/Supply/Sail, doDrawModule 0x4C72BE) are tested on every draw. Integer-frame-equality FXEvents (no FireWhenSkipped), FrameStop ranges, frame-less and ModelConditionState FXEvents, LuaEvent Frame triggers and ParticleSysBone-FX events therefore fire about twice per animation frame in 60 mode. This site moves their evaluation to the B-render only.
sites.evidence:
FUN_004BCE68 (called only from 0x4C7819 in doDrawModule):
- loop 1, state+0x78 FXEvents: fires FUN_004BABBA (FXList at a bone or the object, via 0x4B1B5A/0x494615) when Frame <= (int)cur <= FrameStop or cur == Frame, or Frame < 0 with FrameStep 0 (every draw). Only FireWhenSkipped entries use the prev/cur crossing test 0x4B337B.
- LuaEvent: 0x4B91E2 fires on (int)cur == Frame.
- loop 2, state+0x84 ParticleSysBone-FX: appends PSB entries and sets the +0x48 rebuild flag.
- tail loop at 0x4BD196: state+0xB8 ModelConditionState FXEvents fire on every draw, unconditionally.
The animation frame advances by the W3D sync delta in 0x4BF560, which C3 splits about 16/17 per render. Each integer frame therefore lasts about 2 draws in 60 mode versus about 1 in stock.
AotR data: 3389 FXEvents in total; 768 non-FireWhenSkipped FXEvents in playable objects (gandalf.ini 21, huorn 20, dwalin 16, entwives 15, witchking 12+12+10, elessar 10, corsairship 8; FX_SplatDust on cavalry and riders 101); 5 ModelConditionState FXEvents (baraddur FX_BaradDurWaveDust; khandish/easterling chariot and dwarven battlewagon FX_HordeResurrection) that fire every draw; 31 LuaEvent Frame triggers (troll show_rock/hide_rock).
The FXs contain particle systems, sounds and dynamic decals (for example FX_GandalfPreAttackBlastRealNEW: 4 particle systems plus GandalfSpellVoice; FX_EntFootStep: dust plus footprint decal).
sites.risks:
Design choice (option B). The event FX is spawned on the B-render, the render whose animation frame and bone pose equal stock render k's. This follows the stock timing and positions exactly, but it means B creates FX (particle systems, sounds, decals). These are client-only (nuggets use the client RNG 0x6D32E4/0x6D343B; no logic-RNG callers in the FXList code 0x5D0000-0x5E4000).
Option C, if the team prefers that B never spawns anything: same two addresses with the predicates swapped. Here, INT_FXEV_GATE skips the call on g_skipB, and INT_FXEV_PREV skips the store on g_skipA. Events are then evaluated on A over (a_{n-1}, a_n], which is count-exact but offset by half a step.
Edge cases, both options: a module drawn on only one render of a pair would lose or repeat one window. In normal flow both renders draw the same region with the same camera M_k, and B advances iff A advanced (C3). An iface anim query (0x4C0B1B..0x4C0E73) during B's clientUpdate only runs 0x4BF560 with the B rule, which is consistent.
No 4b form is needed (event-based).

sites.purpose:
Make the terrain tile-texture rebuild budget A-only.

Today every B-render runs the terrain On_Frame_Update. Whenever tiles are pending, it rebuilds up to 2 more 512x512 terrain tile textures on the CPU. Per 33 ms pair that is 3 rebuilds while panning (stock: 1) and 4 while settling (stock: 2). All of the extra work lands on the B-render, which is supposed to be the cheap copy.

This is the render-side cause of 'it stutters for a bit when panning the camera fast'. The fix restores the stock cadence per pair and makes B cheap again, so the pacer can absorb the A-render cost by catching up on B.
sites.evidence:
Scene loop and registration:
- The loop 0x46FF16..0x46FF62 calls vt+0x34 for every object on scene+0x78.
- The terrain (Class_ID 4) is on that list: at 0x465F2C it is registered with scene->vt+0x38(terrain, 0) after scene->vt+0x08 (Add_Render_Object).
- For Class_ID 4 the call is skipped only when byte [[0xDE4690]+0x1914] is set. Only the script and debug setters 0x7BB316 and 0x7BCE53 write it; it is 0 in normal play.
- So On_Frame_Update runs once per scene render, on A and on B.

State machine of 0x4E0A73:
- state = [edi+0x3934].
- 1: state becomes 3, no work.
- 2: budget 1, state becomes 3.
- 3: budget 2.
- If [edi+0x38C0] is set: budget 0x63.
- It loops over the tile grid [+0x3888] ([+0x3890] x [+0x3894] tiles, 0xD4 bytes each). For each tile it calls 0x511F6B, and decrements the budget when that call returns 1 (a texture was built).
- 0x63F3BF (a bare ret) and 0x51577F (an EH-prolog no-op) do no work.
- If budget is left over, state becomes 0 (0x4E0B41).

Setter and callers:
- vt+0x22C = 0x4E0C95 sets state = arg ? 1 : 2.
- W3DView::update calls it at 0x48C6FB with push 0, only after setCameraTransform with [ebp-0xE] set.
- The W3DView vtable function 0x48C774 (slot 0xBDD4EC) calls it at 0x48CA6B.
- Both callers are A-only in 60 mode.

Tile builder 0x511F6B:
- It releases the textures of tiles not flagged visible.
- For a visible tile without a texture it calls 0x4AE3CD(x, y, cells=[tile+0x58], 32 texels/cell, fmt 0x19, 0) and returns 1.
- 0x4AE3CD creates a power-of-two texture (0x4EF2C3) and fills it on the CPU: a per-cell blend (0x4AE772) into A1R5G5B5 per texel, then D3DX9_27 D3DXFilterTexture for the mip chain (0x4EEC82).
- A second texture [tile+0x40] is built the same way when GD+0x49 is set (0x512037..0x5120A3).
- Tiles are 16 cells (0x4E1520 steps by 0x10), so a build is 512x512 at full texture quality. DAT_00DD1E4C values 0, 1, 2+ give 32, 16, 8 texels per cell.

Rendering:
- The tile render 0x5151B7 falls back to a low-res texture [+0x34] until [+0x38] exists.
- The terrain Render 0x4E28F0 and the tile render path 0x4E16A1, 0x4E1520 and 0x5151B7 keep only one-shot dirty flags ([+0x62] geometry rebuild), so they need no gate.
sites.risks:
Render-side texture cache only, so there is no logic, save or determinism effect.

With the site, tiles become sharp at exactly the stock rate per pair: 1 per 33 ms while panning, 2 while settling, and a full refresh on A. Never faster or slower than stock 30 FPS.

The A-render still carries the stock cost of up to 1-2 builds. If a single build takes longer than about 16 ms on the test PC, A still overruns. B is now cheap, though, so the deadline pacer catches up within the pair.

A finer split (1 build on A, 1 on B while settling) is possible by redirecting the immediate at 0x4E0AAB. It is not exact while panning, so it is not recommended.

Not measured at runtime: the cost of a 512x512 CPU blend plus mip build per tile is inferred from the code.

group_notes.render-internal integrators part 1:
All 29 spans checked against a copy of game.dat with pefile and capstone. The bytes are identical in <game folder>/aotr/zGameDats/delayfix.dat and <game folder>/rotwk/game820.dat. No span is near any AotR hook.

Branch-into-span checks used three methods:
- every 0x00xxxxxx operand in listing.asm;
- a scan of the whole image for 4-byte absolute pointers;

Every hit was a false positive from mid-instruction bytes; the details are in each site.

DESIGN ISSUES AND DEVIATIONS FROM PLAN 1.5:
1. Overlay render objects 0x4F6B8D and 0x4F81D7 each have THREE per-Render UV integrators, but the plan and SYNTHESIS list only the 0.03 one (0x4F6C86/0x4F8321). Four sites are added:
   - 0x4F6CA7 and 0x4F8342 (mulss by 0.0225);
   - 0x4F6CC0 and 0x4F835B (x87 fmul qword 0.005; the DLL var must be a double).
   Without them those UVs scroll at 2x on B-renders.
2. Shrubs: 0x4E837E is the shrub render itself (it draws via 0x4E5F64), and it contains a second per-call integrator: push-aside [+0x19B4] += [+0x19B8] at 0x4E852D. Both that integrator and the sway call 0x4E83F9 are gated by the local paused flag [ebp-1]. The site therefore moves to 0x4E83F0, which forces [ebp-1]=1 on B. One site covers both integrators exactly. A gate on the call 0x4E83F9 alone would be insufficient.
3. Decal spiral: the site moves from 0x732A84 to 0x732AA9, for three reasons:
   - EFLAGS from the comiss at 0x732A7C are live across 0x732A84;
   - xmm3 is also a guard operand;
   - an angle integrator was missed (angle += t^2*RPM at 0x732AF6).
   On B the cave zeroes xmm3 and xmm4 after the guards. The angle normaliser 0x644FD0 is the identity for in-range values, so B is bit-exact and redraws A's opacity and rotation.
4. Water river UV is NOT needed in 2a. 0x500137 is reachable only through vtable 0xBDDF90 slot 0x28 (0x4916D9), called only at 0x648833 in GameClient::update, and PLAN 1.4 already gates that A-only. The operand redirects (instead of .rdata writes) are provided as phase 4b, for use only if TerrainVisual::update is ever run on B (G1 U7 open).
5. B-gate predicate: render-internal stubs use g_skipB, defined as g_m60 && g_inB && g_inClientUpdate. C0 writes it on the main thread right before and after the B-render's clientUpdate, and the reset hook and mode-off clear it. Stubs also check fs:[0x24] against g_mainTid, so the load-screen thread is always stock. Inside a render, g_skipB equals !g_uiTick. Unlike raw g_uiTick, it can never gate code running in the stock step after the B-render. All operand-redirect DLL vars switch at exactly the same two points. They must be initialised in DllMain by copying the original constants from game memory, so 30-mode results are bit-identical.
6. Shared stubs: STUB_INC_DD1BEC (4 sites), STUB_INC_DD1A40 (2 sites), STUB_INC_DD1BFC (2 sites). 0x4F5C8D differs from the others: the INC is followed by cvtsi2ss, not cmp, so XMM0 and EAX are live and EFLAGS are dead. The stubs touch no SSE or x87.

PHASE 4b SUMMARY:
- Exact integer half-step: shore waves (A +16, B +17; the cave is already 4b-ready through g_shoreStepA/B).
- Linear float steps (overlay frame and UVs, 0.05 scrolls, river): the same operand vars at c/2 on both A and B. The constant is halved exactly; the sum differs from stock only by float rounding; visual only.
- Decal: approximate only (0.5 scaling on both renders).
- No exact form, stay A-only: INC view-filter counters, material x0.8, recoil, motion-blur counter, trees and shrubs.

Open item: the shrub 30-entry round-robin visibility refresh (0x4E8423..0x4E8454) still runs on B. It is a cache refresh, not a time integrator, and visual only. A 9-byte detour at 0x4E841A could skip it on B if exactness is wanted.

group_notes.pacing/present:
All bytes were verified with pefile and capstone against a copy of game.dat. Its SHA-256 is cc08275d…705dc, the same as rotwk\game.dat. Every span, and the code around each resume point, is byte-identical in aotr\zGameDats\delayfix.dat and rotwk\game820.dat. None of the spans touches an AotR hook. The branch-into-span check used three passes over all executable sections, including .danetta and .angmar: a listing.asm operand regex, a scan of the whole image for 32-bit absolute pointers, and a capstone linear sweep. None of them found a branch into any span interior.

1. PACER exit. 0x63A1F5 is the right exit: it is the stock "waited" exit. It runs `mov esi,[ebp-0x20]` (engine; [ebp-0x20] is set at 0x639D18), then `mov [0xDE4318],edi` (last frame time), then `jmp 0x63A21F`. At 0x63A21F the code calls the watchdog 0x631D04 when [0xDE42F8]!=0 and jumps to the loop head 0x639EC6. That loop head needs ESI=engine and EBX=0, and EDI is dead there. Exiting through 0x63A21F would also work, but then the cave would have to write [0xDE4318] itself and keep ESI correct. Leaving through 0x63A1F5 with EDI=timeGetTime() keeps the stock limiter correct after a switch from 60 back to 30. The x87 stack is empty at 0x63A196 (the code before it is SSE only) and at 0x63A1F5. On entry ESI=engine; at 0x63A1B2 the stock code overwrites ESI with P, which is why 0x63A1F5 reloads it.

2. Design issue: M>1 on a 60 Hz vsync display. During M>1 the limiter is off ([0xDE4320]=0), so the pacer and its Present-skip rule never run. A drawn A and its mirrored B then give 2 Presents per 29 ms, which is 69 per second. In fullscreen FIFO at 60 Hz, Present blocks, and the M>1 stretches run about 13% slower than stock. That breaks the PLAN §4.2 rule that an M>1 cinematic has the same logic frames per wall-second as stock. Fix, folded into the PRESENT rule: always skip the B-render's Present when its A drew with M>1 (g_mDrawRid==g_renderId-1 && g_mDrawAM>1). The B still runs drawFrame, so state stays exact. These forced skips should be left out of the fallback skip ratio.

3. Change from the 0x44B964-only site. The M>1 site is widened to 0x44B95F (24 bytes). The multiplier W3DView+0x23D4 can change inside A's drawFrame (the camera-path lerp writes it at 0x48A69A, inside updateCameraMovements). A hook only at 0x44B964 cannot see an A-draw that took the M<=1 branch, so a B with M>1 would read a stale decision. With the wider span, A records its decision on both branches, and B mirrors A whatever its own M is. The record is tied to the render id, so A-renders that left the function earlier (the IsIconic exit at 0x44B7AD, the fast-forward exit at 0x44B8EF) make their B skip, exactly as stock render k did not draw.

4. The B-render must set ESI=[0xBD089C] as well as EAX. That value is USER32!ClientToScreen, which the capture path calls with `call esi` at 0x44BA4B/0x44BA6F when [0xDC7568]>0 && GD+0xEA0!=0. The review's fix set only EAX. In normal 60-mode play (M<=1) the B-render now also jumps straight to 0x44B9E3. This matches stock, because for M<=1 the stock wait does nothing (prev=now−30 gives elapsed 30 >= 29). As a result [0xDC7700], which is read only by the M>1 wait, is written by A-renders only.

5. The draw do-while 0x44BBFE..0x44BC20 jumps back to 0x44B9A8, after the MDRAW span. It can never repeat in retail: drawFrame returns 0 whenever GL+0x124 (paused) is set (0x44A262), and the loop needs that flag. So a B-render, whose camera is frozen by S1, cannot hang there. This confirms CRITIC K1.

6. Gap markers.
   - Device lost: no extra site is needed. The Sleep(200) branch at 0x522696 and the Reset_Device(1) branch at 0x52268F are reached only after Present at this call returned 0x88760868. So the PRESENT stub sets g_gapDevLost there, at no extra byte cost.
   - Optional explicit site, if wanted: 0x522696, 10 bytes `68 c8 00 00 00 e8 90 61 09 00` (push 0xC8; call 0x5B8830 = Sleep wrapper) → `e9 <rel32:GAP_SLEEP_CAVE> 90 90 90 90 90`. The cave does `mov byte [g_gapDevLost],1; push 0xC8; call 0x5B8830; jmp 0x5226A0`. The argument stays on the stack and is popped by `add esp,4` at 0x5226AC; EFLAGS are dead. No branch lands in 0x522697..0x52269F. The span start is the target of the jne at 0x52268B.
   - Reset_Device: func_detour GAP_RESET at 0x522000 (6 bytes).
   - Recommendation: the pacer should also treat any single overrun far above T (for example >250 ms or >8·T) as a gap without debt. That covers the minimise loop 0x44181F (Sleep(5)), alt-tab and debugger stalls.

7. LOD. Gating the one sample call at 0x44B7B3 is enough, and 0x4438DA needs no patch. 0x601F94 is a pure lookup, and 0x6020E7 only acts when [mgr+0x176C] changes. On a B-render the average Display+0x180 is unchanged, so that call does nothing. Halding the value passed to 0x4438F6 instead would only approximate the per-pair average, so I rejected it. The engine's debug FPS readout will show about 30 in 60 mode.

8. Contracts this group needs from others:
   - C0 increments g_renderId exactly once per main-loop iteration, in all modes, before clientUpdate.
   - g_inB is set for the whole B iteration, on the main thread only.
   - g_mainTid is recorded at the first C0.
   - The mode controller and the reset hook leave g_m60 live, as PLAN says.
   - Stubs check the thread with `mov ecx,fs:[0x24]`, the WoW64 TEB32 thread id that GetCurrentThreadId reads. ECX is dead at both sites that use it.

9. In the PRESENT stub, the 30-mode path keeps the original `push ebx` x4 (EBX==0 from 0x5225F6). A skipped Present returns S_OK and takes the stock success path. That path increments [0xDD34C4], a stats counter read only at 0x5225FF, and clears [0xDD1F38], which nothing in the listing reads.

10. AotR60_Pacer should compute P in single precision, `(int)(1000.0f/((float)fps*mult))`. That equals the stock fild/fmul/fdivr/_ftol2 result under the forced 24-bit x87 precision, without touching the control word.

2. Calling conventions.
   - Set_Transform:
     - Virtual slot vt+0x54 of camera vtable 0xBE8748, = 0x533550. Thiscall, ECX=CameraClass*, [esp+4]=const Matrix3D* (12 floats, 3x4 row-major, translation at m[3], m[7], m[11]), ret 4.

     - Thiscall, ECX=cam, [esp+4]=hfov (radians), [esp+8]=vfov, where -1.0 means derive it from the aspect at +0xE8. ret 8.
     - Uses x87 fptan, so its result depends on the game's 24-bit control word. Writes +0xD8=-tan(h/2), +0xE0=tan(h/2), +0xDC=-tv, +0xE4=tv, +0xE8 (aspect, only when vfov is given) and +0xFC=0.

   - Set_Clip_Planes 0x5337C0: thiscall(znear, zfar), ret 8, writes +0xEC/+0xF0 and +0xFC=0.
   - Update_Frustum 0x533B70 rebuilds the frustum at +0x100 and the projection/inverse caches when +0xFC==0.

group_notes.other A-only gates:
The group is fully specified: three phase-2a sites, one optional telemetry site, and coverage of all 53 calls in InGameUI::update. I wrote no files.

1. Gate condition differs from the PLAN wording. PLAN and G7 say to skip when `g_m60 && !g_uiTick`. But g_uiTick stays 0 for the whole Y iteration, including the stock logic step that follows the B-render. A callee-side gate keyed only on g_uiTick would therefore also skip a call that comes from logic. All three stubs instead skip only when all of these hold: g_m60, !g_uiTick, g_inClientUpdate, and the current thread (fs:[0x24]) is g_mainTid. That is the same as g_inB on the main thread. C0 must maintain g_inClientUpdate and g_mainTid in every mode, as PLAN §1.3 already says. A shared `B_RENDER_NOW` predicate or a precomputed g_skipA byte is fine, as long as all callee gates and isTick use the same definition.
